hook: Solomon's path from electrical engineering to venture investment to AI partnerships at Airbus traces the evolution of applied AI from semiconductor and IoT adjacencies into aerospace's core technology strategy. At Airbus she shapes the partnerships and technology decisions that will determine how autonomous systems, AI-assisted design, and intelligent maintenance enter one of the most safety-critical industries in the world.
name: Reena Solomon

quote.text: Leading partnerships and technology strategy for AI and autonomy to shape the future of aerospace.

moniker: Head of AI Partnerships at Airbus, North America

reading.body:
Reena Solomon's career maps the path that applied AI takes from hardware and semiconductors into safety-critical physical systems, ending at Airbus where she now governs how AI and autonomy enter commercial aviation.

Her background is technical before it is strategic. An electrical engineering degree from Clemson preceded an MBA and then roles that moved through semiconductors, IoT, autonomous vehicles, and robotics, first as an investor conducting due diligence at SK Telecom Ventures, then as the person who built Samsung's robotics initiative from concept to product definition. That sequence matters because aerospace AI is not primarily a software problem. Autonomous systems and AI-assisted design in aircraft manufacturing depend on hardware reliability, sensor integration, and regulatory tolerance for failure, all domains where her earlier work is directly relevant.

The data does not say which specific AI partnerships Solomon has formed at Airbus, what technologies she has selected, or how Airbus's AI investment compares to competitors. Her role title and stated mission are on record, but outcomes at Airbus are not covered here. What the record does show is a career that accumulated expertise in exactly the adjacencies, venture scouting, robotics strategy, autonomous systems, that aerospace needs as it decides how much AI to absorb and how fast.
